@graph.headline: The EU AI Act has several dates—not one delayed deadline
@graph.description: A practical guide to the AI Act's separate 2026, 2027 and 2028 dates, including Article 50 transitions and high-risk system categories.

acceptedAnswer.text: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the AI Omnibus amendment, entered into force on 27 July 2026. It amended the AI Act’s timetable for specified obligations rather than replacing the Act’s overall schedule. Article 113 now sets distinct dates for new Article 5 provisions, an Article 50(2) transition and two high-risk system categories.

mainEntity.name: Does the 2 December 2026 date defer all Article 50 duties?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The transition in amended Article 113 applies to providers’ Article 50(2) marking duties for systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026. Article 50 contains other transparency obligations with their own scope. The transition should not be described as a blanket extension for every Article 50 requirement.

mainEntity.name: Which high-risk systems follow the 2027 date?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chapter III Sections 1–3 apply from 2 December 2027 to systems classified under Article 6(2) and listed in Annex III. This date is tied to that legal route, not to every system described informally as high-risk. Classification depends on the statutory conditions and the system’s intended purpose.

The 2 August 2028 date applies to relevant Article 6(1) systems connected to products covered by the Annex I legislation and subject to the specified third-party conformity assessment. It is not a general extension for all software, devices or AI-enabled products. The legal classification tests still control.

mainEntity.name: Is this legal advice for a specific product?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This is a dated explainer of the application schedule, not a legal opinion or product classification. Determining whether a particular system is prohibited, high-risk, in transition or exempt requires facts about its purpose, market status, role in a product and applicable legal conditions. The Official Journal text controls.
